entry.title: SAC Story filter error: 0BI_ALL required, but SAC Analyzer works fine - what is the root cause? Gap?
entry.content:
Dear SAC Experts,

my customer reported a strange behaviour in a SAC Story, with an underlying BW live query.... and we have no idea about the root cause or the solution.

Let me first explain, what works:

The BW user has sufficient BW authorization to:

- open the query sucessfully in RSRT (the auth. variable for Company Code is pre-filled in the variable screen)

- open the query in the SAC Analyzer and navigate here

- open the story and see data in the table widget in a SAC story.

But as soon as the user tries to change any random dimension filter of this live query, the content does not load but instead a red exclamation mark appears with error message for insufficient authorization.

When we check SU53, we can see one entry like this for each and every tried filter:

There is absolutely no reason for the need of 0BI_ALL, since the user HAS sufficient priviliges, like proved 3 times (see above).

Has anyone of you seen this issue before?

It is BW 7.5 on Prem with SP33 ... and like said, everything in data selection to display works fine... just the filters don't.

I feel there is AGAIN a feature gap between SAC Analyzer and SAC Story table widget.

For a "similar" issue, where I can use a Bex Condition in the Analyzer but not in the story table, I have opened an incident, which is still in progress for more than 6 weeks now ... with pure ticket ping-pong instead that the support would just look up their "Feature gap list" and tell me "Yes, you are right, it is missing functionality" 😞 it is annoying.

Please help me out, to avoid opening one more "feature gap" incident, which will take weeks.

Update: After tracing (not successful) and testing for preparing the ticket text ... I found out a "strange" workaround:

As soon as I include the dimension, which is authorization-relevant into the story filter, then all over sudden all other filters work without any error message ... that means there is a difference in reading regular attributes with provided auth. value vs. not.

(I wish SAC or BW developers would read here and recognize the bug ... but I doubt it)

Thanks a lot, Martin

entry.title: RAW → Harmonization → Reporting: Where should Business Logic live?
entry.content:
A common approach is:
RAW → HARMONIZATION → REPORTING → SAC

On paper, this separation looks straightforward. But in real implementation projects, the boundaries between these layers can become less obvious.

One question I’ve been thinking about while working with SAP Datasphere: Where should business logic actually live in Raw, Harmonization, or Reporting?

For example:
COGS should be calculated from specific GL accounts, with sign inversion and certain account mappings applied.

Would you typically implement that logic in the HARMONIZATION layer, so it becomes reusable across multiple reports?

Or would you keep harmonization closer to the source data and implement the business rule in the REPORTING/Analytical Model layer, where it is directly tied to the reporting requirement?

I'm particularly interested in real project experience here.

Have you encountered cases where putting business logic in the wrong layer caused problems later, such as duplicated logic, inconsistent KPIs, performance issues, or having to redesign the model close to go-live?

Are there any Datasphere-specific limitations or best practices that influence where you place this logic?

Would love to hear how others approach this in actual implementations.

Thanks.

entry.title: SAC Planning – Cash Calculation Across Planning Models
entry.content:
Hi everyone,

We are implementing SAC Planning for a retail customer whose requirement is for cash in the Balance Sheet to reflect planning activities across Sales, OPEX, and CAPEX.

For example, sales are assumed to be cash sales. In OPEX, an expense incurred in January is recognized in the P&L and creates an accrued liability, while the cash payment occurs in February based on DPO assumptions. Similarly, CAPEX planning should reflect the timing of asset payments and their impact on cash.

I reviewed the standard business content and noticed that cash is calculated through the Cash Flow and then reflected in the Balance Sheet.

Should we follow this standard approach, or does the customer's requirement to reflect cash impacts directly from each planning model introduce duplicate calculations and unnecessary complexity? How should we design this to ensure accurate cash movements without double counting across the P&L, Balance Sheet, and Cash Flow?

Thank you.

 

 

 @achab @XiwenLiao  SAP Analytics Cloud for planning

entry.title: SAC Planning – Cash flow Calculation logic that affects cash in the balance sheet
entry.content:
Hi SAP Community,

I was initially infomed that the Cash balance in the Balance Sheet is derived from the Cash Flow calculation, so I started tracing the logic in SAP_FI_FPA_S4 to understand how the Cash Flow Statement is calculated and how it drives the Balance Sheet cash balance.

However, I am currently stuck on the calculation logic behind the individual cash flow movements, as below:

 

 

 

In Step 10 of the third Data Action, (SAP_FI_FPA_S4_Finance_Planning_Admin4_PlanningTrigger), I noticed that the logic for Change in Provisions (Account 1000310) and Change in Accounts Payable (Account 1000350) appears to act as a transfer/mapping layer. The script deletes the existing target account and writes the value again using RESULTLOOKUP (), without explicitly calculating the movement between opening and closing balances.

For example, if opening provisions are 100,000 and closing provisions are 130,000, I would expect the Change in Provisions to be 30,000. However, I could not identify where this difference is calculated, either in this Data Action or in the relevant account formula in the Financial Planning model.

My questions are:

  1. Where are these cash flow movements calculated in the standard SAP Rapid S/4HANA Finance Planning content?

  2. Are the differences between opening and closing balances calculated in an earlier Data Action or another step, or does this logic simply transfer movements that have already been calculated elsewhere?

  3. If the calculation happens elsewhere, which Data Action or model logic should I investigate?

  4. How exactly is the calculated cash flow used to derive or update the Cash balance in the Balance Sheet?

I have attached screenshots below showing the relevant Data Action logic and account configuration for reference.

I have been tracing this logic for the last two days, so I would really appreciate any guidance on where the actual calculations take place and how the Cash Flow Statement is linked to the Balance Sheet cash balance.

Thanks in advance for your help!

@JefB  @achab SAP Analytics Cloud for planning

entry.title: SAC Story: unexpected “Sign in to access this site” popup and “FailedAction – persistedInAConsumer.v
entry.content:
Hello community,

We are facing a recurring issue in SAP Analytics Cloud when working on stories (Optimized Story Experience).

While we refresh a story or edit a story in Edit mode, two things happen:

  1. The browser shows a native “Sign in to access this site” popup that asks for a username and password for the SAC tenant URL (see screenshot 1). 
  2. At the same time, or right after, SAC shows the following error (see screenshot 2):
 
[FailedAction - Action: persistedInAConsumer.v1.preprocessBeforePersist ...]
Error: Store.UnhandledError/Uncaught exception while handling saga

Workaround: The only thing that works is to refresh the browser (F5). This brings the story back, but all unsaved changes are lost. 

thank you!
